- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.27) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior period), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above prior peak or use 2-period moving average for smoothing.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.80) and price is rising, model frequently overreacts; apply downward bias of 0.5–1.5% to forecast if sentiment >0.75.
- Model underestimates when sentiment is mixed (0.27–0.53) and price is trending upward; adjust forecast upward by 0.5–1.5% if sentiment >0.4.
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture mean reversion; if price deviates >2SD from 18-day moving average, apply correction toward mean.
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.00 values, model tends to ignore sentiment and overpredict; reduce forecast by 1–2% if sentiment is 0 for 3+ consecutive days.
